text.zh: 梵高住进疗养院后，早餐后在花园里一眼看到了这丛刚开的鸢尾，很快就开始画它。
text.en: Soon after arriving at the asylum, he spotted these irises in flower in the garden after breakfast, and soon began to paint them.

text.zh: 这些蓝色的鸢尾原本是紫色的，是用蓝色和红色颜料混出来的。红色褪了，就变成了今天的蓝。
text.en: These blue irises were once violet, mixed from blue and red pigments. As the red faded, they turned blue.

label.zh: 卧室的墙也是这样褪色的
label.en: The bedroom walls faded the same way

text.zh: 在一片蓝紫色里，有一朵白色的鸢尾。
text.en: Among all the blue and violet, there is a single white iris.

text.zh: 到疗养院两周后，他写信告诉提奥：“考虑到生活主要是在花园里，这里并不那么悲伤。”
text.en: Two weeks after arriving, he wrote to Theo: "Considering that life happens above all in the garden, it isn't so sad."

text.zh: 梵高把作画称为“疾病的避雷针”。他相信，只要继续画画，就能保护自己。
text.en: Van Gogh called painting "the lightning conductor for my illness". He believed that as long as he kept painting, it would protect him.

text.zh: 提奥把这幅画送去巴黎展览，写信告诉梵高：“它从远处就吸引人的目光，是一幅充满空气和生命的美丽习作。”
text.en: Theo sent the painting to an exhibition in Paris and wrote to Vincent: "It strikes the eye from afar. It is a beautiful study full of air and life."

text.zh: 1889年5月，梵高自愿住进圣雷米的疗养院。刚到不久，他就在花园里画下了这丛鸢尾。
text.en: In May 1889, Van Gogh voluntarily entered the asylum at Saint-Rémy. Soon after arriving, he painted this clump of irises in the garden.

caption.en: May 1889 · J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles

title.zh: 第二幕 · 第一次展览

text.zh: 那年9月，提奥把它送到巴黎的独立艺术家沙龙。这是梵高第一次参加公开展览的两幅作品之一。它的第一位主人是评论家奥克塔夫·米尔博，他写道：“他多么懂得花的精妙！”
text.en: That September, Theo sent it to the Salon des Indépendants in Paris, one of two works in Van Gogh's first public exhibition. Its first owner, the critic Octave Mirbeau, wrote: "How well he understood the exquisite nature of flowers!"

alt.en: Vincent van Gogh, Irises, 1889, J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles

caption.en: May 1889 · J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles

text.zh: 整整一年后，他又在鸢尾开得最好的时候画了一次。1990年，盖蒂博物馆买下了这幅画。
text.en: Exactly a year later, he painted irises again, when they were at their best. In 1990, the Getty Museum acquired this painting.

final.zh: 考虑到生活主要是在花园里，这里并不那么悲伤。
final.en: Considering that life happens above all in the garden, it isn't so sad.
